title: Michael Carrick backs Luke Shaw to make England’s World Cup squad
content:
Michael Carrick has backed Luke Shaw to make the cut for England’s World Cup squad when Thomas Tuchel names his selection on Friday.

Shaw last played for England in the final of the 2024 European Championship, and was not under consideration last season as he experienced repeated injury issues.

But he has been fit throughout this campaign and is the only United player to start every Premier League game. He scored his first goal for United in more than three years by sweeping in a sweet left-foot strike against Nottingham Forest on his 37th appearance of the season, helping his team to win 3-2.

Afterwards, Carrick was full of praise for his left-back and made a case for Tuchel taking him to the United States, Canada and Mexico. “I certainly think so, yeah,” Carrick said. “I haven’t got much sway in the matter at all, but I certainly think so.

“Again, the consistency, just what he’s capable of doing, the performance, the experience, his strengths, his attributes that he’s got. For me, he’s a fantastic full-back.”

On Shaw’s ever-present availability, Carrick added: “I think it’s difficult for anybody to do to be honest. When there’s so many games it’s not an easy thing to be able to, sometimes it’s no fault of your own.

“Unfortunately injuries are part of football and there’s other things that come into play. So to start every game is really fantastic.

“Next season is a new season, there’s different types of runs of game so that’s part of adapting but then he’ll be a little bit older and experience in knowing your body and managing things.

“He’s at that stage now where he’s got an awful lot of experience, he’s been here for a long time, he knows the club, he know what it feels like, he knowns the ups and he’s suffered some of the more challenging times. So next season I think his experience will be valuable, however many games he plays.”
